recentItems.title: KGSW Commercial Breaks, 12/11/1987
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Commercial breaks taken during the 8 O'Clock Movie presentation of "Thunderbolt and Lightfoot" on then-Fox affiliate KGSW in Albuquerque, New Mexico. 

The station no longer exists as it went off the air in 1993. KGSW's ownership bought KKTO channel 2 in 1992 and moved its programming there the following year under the call letters KASA, using KGSW's studios and staff. Channel 14's license was then surrendered to the FCC. A few years later, channel 14 signed back on as a PAX station, then flipped to Telefutura, and is now the market's Univision affiliate. Channel 2 was sold to KRQE owners LIN in 2006, then off to Ramar Communications in 2017 due to Nexstar purchasing Media General (which had bought LIN), who made it a Telemundo station which it remains now but owned by the network.

FOX moved to KRQE's second subchannel in 2017 (but had rebranded as FOX New Mexico a year earlier in anticipation of the move).

Record date: Friday, December 11, 1987

recentItems.title: KKTO Station Break, 9/24/1989
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Quick station break (with all promos, no ads) taken from in between an airing of "Kenneth Copeland" and "Jimmy Swaggart" on independent station KKTO-TV, channel 2, in Santa Fe, New Mexico and serving the Albuquerque market.

This is pretty rare footage of the station's time as KKTO. The station, which had previously been known as KNMZ, and of which footage is just as rare, was bought a year earlier by Coronado Communications, a holding company of Sunbelt Communications, which was the longtime owner of Las Vegas NBC affiliate KVBC (now Sinclair-owned NBC affiliate KSNV). The calls had just changed to KKTO a couple of weeks before this had been recorded, and the local newspaper, which was used to date this clip, still had been calling the station KNMZ.

To match its new Vegas sister station, KKTO adopted a similar logo to KVBC, as well as its announcer, Al Vanik.

KKTO would be a relatively short lived station, facing financial issues as the Albuquerque market could not support two commercial independents at this time. It wouldn't be until the netlet era and 1995 when channel 50 hit the airwaves that a competitor to the local Fox affiliate would finally become viable.

In 1992, KGSW (local Fox affiliate at the time)'s owner Providence Journal bought KKTO from Coronado and moved the KGSW programming on to channel 2, along with moving its transmitter to the same Sandia Crest site the other local affiliates use. The call letters were changed to KASA to signify a new start. KGSW then signed off channel 14 and would remain silent for six years before PAX bought channel 14 and signed that back on. 

Today: channel 2 is a Telemundo O&O (still called KASA), channel 14 is now a Univision affiliate, and FOX is now on the second channel of CBS affiliate KRQE (as if the channel 2 history wasn't confusing enough). This is all due to corporate mergers of these TV giants.

Date recorded: Sunday, September 24, 1989

recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Commercial breaks taken during part 1 of "Oldest Living Confederate Widow Tells All" on CBS affiliate WGNX in Atlanta, Georgia.

Then owned by Tribune, WGNX replaced WAGA, channel 5, as Atlanta's CBS affiliate following the New World transaction. Fox made a deal with them in which nearly all of their stations switched to Fox. Fox had been on channel 36, WATL.

Both WATL and WGNX had passed on CBS originally, so CBS bought WVEU, channel 69, with the intention of making that their new home. However, CBS preferred being on a higher-profile station. Finally, Tribune gave in about a month before the affiliation switch was to happen. They already were airing local news, which began in 1989 while WGNX was still independent. Tribune swapped WGNX to Meredith in 1999 for KCPQ in Seattle.

The station would continue its rotating identities until current owner Gray gave up CBS in September 2025. Channel 69, now called WUPA, took the affiliation as a result, and so this station is once again independent.

recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Commercial breaks taken during the Raycom Sports presentation of NFL preseason game New Orleans Saints vs. Houston Oilers on Paramount-owned Fox affiliate KRRT in San Antonio, Texas (licensed to Kerrville).

This was a pretty historic event for San Antonio as it would be the first football game to be played at the then-brand new Alamodome. Built mainly to lure an NFL team to San Antonio, this never happened (and probably never will) for a few reasons. Instead, the arena has served mainly as a venue for concerts, lower-level football, and high school graduations. It was also the main home of the Spurs from 1993 until they left for a purpose built arena in 2002 (what's now the Frost Bank Center). The Cowboys would also hold several training camps here over the years but have decided to hold that in California for over a decade now.

In 1995, Fox moved its affiliation to present affiliate KABB, with KRRT becoming UPN, WB, MyNetworkTV, CW, and now Dabl in that order. The station's call letters became the present KMYS in 2006 when they lost WB, and the then-new CW network, to KCWX (though Sinclair was apparently favoring MyNet over CW for their stations, and likely passed on CW for KMYS, mainly taking CW when MyNet wasn't available).

recentItems.title: KVDA Telenoticias San Antonio a las 10:00 (Full), 4/26/2013
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — https://bit.ly/S31MA

Complete (except for the first few seconds of the tease) 10pm newscast from the Telemundo affiliate in San Antonio. Recorded Friday, April 26, 2013.

KVDA has been owned by Telemundo from almost the start (since 1990), however in 2009, NBC signed a contract with ZGS Communications, then its largest affiliate group, to operate KVDA and its Fresno sister station. NBC took back control to KVDA in 2014, a precursor to them purchasing that company outright three years later.

KVDA has long had a rocky history with local news, long playing second fiddle to Univision's KWEX, the market's, and nation's, first Spanish-language television station. KVDA has experimented with different formats and timeslots of news over the years before the original news operation shut down in 2007, replaced first by a regional newscast produced by Dallas' KXTX, and a couple years later by a locally-focused newscast produced by KXTX and using local news video via an agreement with KENS.

In 2012, ZGS started the current news operation, which has been its most successful effort to date. This was not the original graphics and music package used. It originally borrowed music from sister station WTMO and used a more red/blue graphics scheme. Earlier in 2013, the station began using this which aligned them more with the O&Os.

In 2015, the station began to use the O&O graphics and music of the time. NBC also made several technical and talent changes to the product. The set here was heavily renovated, then completely replaced. NBC has also expanded the station's output to middays, 4pm, and weekends as well. KVDA is the closest it has ever been to KWEX in ratings, but still trails them significantly due to brand loyalty to Univision in the city that gave them their start.

The graphics are Telemundo's then-O&O graphics package, while the music is "Telemundo News" by Cacharros Musik. The voiceover artist is unknown but NBC also replaced him.

Anchored by Esmeralda Medellin, weather from Lilian Perez (the last member from the 2012 launch still with the station today), and sports anchored by Jaime Becerril (who awkwardly has to do his interviews in English then quickly translate it back into Spanish for the audience). Includes reports from Lori Montenegro (Telemundo), Geraldine Ortega, Ciro Villarreal, Jazive Perez (Telemundo), and Ana Cecilia Mendez (Telemundo).

Commercials will be uploaded separately at a later date.

Latter half of the 12pm newscast from the CBS affiliate in San Antonio, Texas, recorded on Monday, June 25, 2001.

Unfortunately there's no open or A-block here, but a good chunk of the rest of the newscast including the close are featured here. It starts in the middle of a CBS News package and continues right through the end.

The theme music was "One World" from Stephen Arnold Music, which the station commissioned in 1998 and kept for six years. Graphics were done by EQ Vance and also debuted in 1998 upon Belo's takeover of the station. Those lasted until 2002 when the station began producing their graphics in-house (many promos already began to feature in-house produced graphics that didn't really match the news look). Voiceover artist was Bill Ratner, who had just taken over from Jeff David.

Anchored by KENS legend Fred Lozano, Cindy Casiano, and weather from Bill Taylor, the only one still with the station today (Taylor would be promoted to weather chief in 2003, following the firing of Albert Flores).

A report is included from Christy Feig (CBS News).
